trust_decision.summary: Rodauth skips its CSRF token check when it classifies a request as JSON (assuming that a cross-origin JSON request needs a CORS preflight). The classification is an unanchored Content-Type regexp in json_request?, consumed by the json feature's check_csrf? override before route dispatch.

landing_point.why: The advisory title says 'CSRF bypass via Content-Type'. Grepping for content_type finds only json_request_content_type_regexp, and the fix is a one-character anchor there.

fix_sites.entry_point: Every Rodauth HTTP route (POST /login, /create-account, /change-password, etc.) via the route wrapper at lib/rodauth.rb:166-169 calling check_csrf? -> use_json? -> json_request?

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The demo-site app's own CSRF gate (demo-site/rodauth_demo.rb:97) uses the same unanchored /application\/json/ match. A solver could dismiss it as a demo app that is not part of the shipped gem.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate JSON clients must still be classified as JSON without a CSRF token. That covers 'application/json; charset=utf-8' and 'application/vnd.api+json'. An over-broad fix (exact string equality, or always requiring CSRF) breaks the JSON/JWT API. The jwt feature also treats any non-Basic/Digest Authorization header as JSON.

O6_input_shapes: Content-Type with application/json as a parameter of a CORS-safelisted type (e.g. 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded; application/json'), per fix.diff:504
application/vnd.api+json variant kept by the same regexp (fix.diff:487)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The demo app's global CSRF gate skips check_csrf! when CONTENT_TYPE matches the unanchored /application\/json/, the same mechanism as the fixed regexp; the fix did not touch it
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Demo/sample application, not library code shipped in the gem

O8b_injection_room.sibling: jwt overrides use_json?. A planted jwt-specific content-type check (e.g. a jwt_request_content_type_regexp, or a request.media_type =~ /json/ fallback) would also feed check_csrf? through use_json?
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: jwt already overrides use_json? and historically owned json_request_content_type_regexp itself (doc/CHANGELOG.old:257). A separate jwt-level JSON detector is a plausible maintainer choice.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second JSON classification helper in another feature that some other code path consults for CSRF or JSON-mode decisions
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: internal_request already overrides only_json?, so JSON-mode decisions are already spread across features.

O9_family: CSRF / content-type classification (parser differential on Content-Type)

O10_build.toolchain: Ruby + bundler (roda, sequel, jwt, rack, minitest); specs use SQLite by default
O10_build.project_tests: spec/json_spec.rb, spec/jwt_cors_spec.rb, spec/jwt_spec.rb (driven via spec/spec_helper.rb json_request helper)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Anchor the regexp with \A (exactly the published fix); a wrong fix would compare the content type for exact equality with 'application/json' and break charset/vnd.api+json clients.

out_of_scope_notes: The same 2.47.0 release fixes many unrelated advisories (return-to open redirect, jwt_refresh non-POST, otp drift reuse, token race conditions); those are not screened here.
json_accept_regexp (lib/rodauth/features/json.rb:9) is also unanchored, but it only gates a 406 response, not CSRF.
unverified: Repo size not measured; tiny_repo is assumed from a small Ruby gem (lib/ plus docs).

O8 demo-site route: whether it counts as the 'same protected sink' is a judgement call (it protects the demo's non-Rodauth routes plus Rodauth routes, which also run their own check). Present in latest: unknown (no latest provided).

jwt.rb:83,96-98: any Authorization header other than Basic/Digest (e.g. browser-auto-sent Negotiate) makes use_json? true and skips CSRF. It likely fails later on JWT decode (jwt.rb:41-43), but this was not verified.
Roda's json_parser and route_csrf plugin behaviour (outside this repo) was not inspected.
